name: Telford Spring
coordinateNote: Spring position from OpenStreetMap; the boat ramp is about 150 yards away at the end of 203rd Road.
navigationNote: Drive to the Telford boat ramp at the end of 203rd Road near Luraville. Park on the unpaved road shoulder. The spring lies about 150 yards away.
experience: A second-magnitude spring in a limestone bowl at the river edge, with a sandy bank and a big cypress with spread-out roots behind it. When the Suwannee is low the pool is clear blue and the limestone ledges stand out; when the river is high, dark river water floods over it and it can disappear. It is a known cave-dive site too.
cost: No launch fee. Separate spring admission unconfirmed.
access: Take SR 51 to Luraville, turn on 180th Street, then 203rd Road to its end at the public boat ramp. Parking is a few spots on the road shoulder, unpaved. Day use only, sunrise to sunset. No staff, no lifeguard, no restrooms found. Check the Suwannee river level first: it is only worth the drive when the river is low.

conditions.summary: The water district reports opening the spring to the public in July 2024. FWC lists daytime ramp use; today’s river level, clarity and water entry remain unconfirmed.

water: No dated live visibility report established; clear-spring descriptions are general.
mobility: Road/ramp and natural spring tract have different access; exact parking/walk/water entry unknown.

name: Seminole State Forest: Black Water Creek paddle and spring-fed streams
coordinateNote: Entrance or parking coordinates from the November 12, 2026 gap review.
navigationDestination: Seminole State Forest Cassia Trailhead, Brantley Branch Road just east of SR 44, Cassia, FL 32736
navigationNote: Drive to the listed entrance; follow the access description on arrival.
experience: Hand-launch onto Black Water Creek north of the Sand Road concrete bridge for a quiet wild-stream paddle, or hike to small clear springs such as Sharks Tooth Spring (fifth magnitude, no pool, a run 2 ft wide). Bear Pond trailhead off SR 46 reaches the Lower Wekiva loop.
cost: $2 state forest day pass (buy through ReserveAmerica or 1-877-879-3859; not sold at the office)
access: Sunrise to sunset. The creek launch is reachable only when Sand Road is open (check road condition with the visitor center). Hand-launched craft only; petroleum motors prohibited.
